newsitem.title: BURUNDI: 30 Burundi prisoners killed in November - official.
newsitem.headline: 30 Burundi prisoners killed in November - official.

text.p: A local Burundian official said on Sunday that 30 prisoners, arrested for colluding with anti-government rebels, were killed when they attacked guards at a prison in November.

The comments by Lieutenant-Colonel Boniface Bamuma, governor of Muyinga province close to the Tanzania border, were the first confirmation of the incident at Gisanze prison northeast of the capital Bujumbura.
But he denied reports by travellers from the area who said in Bujumbura on Sunday that 68 prisoners had been killed and buried in a mass grave.
Bamuma told a local radio station the incident started when fighting broke out among prisoners who were under the influence of drugs.
"When the military intervened, the prisoners attacked them. The soldiers defended themselves," he said. Thirty prisoners were killed, he said.
Muyinga province has been the scene of military activity to prevent Hutu anti-government rebels from infiltrating from hideouts in Tanzania.
The Burundian army, dominated by the Tutsi ethnic minority, staged a military coup last July to oust the government led by Hutus who constitute the majority of the population.
Neighbouring African states have refused to recognise the government of Tutsi Major Pierre Buyoya.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in Burundi since the killing of its first freely-elected Hutu president Melchior Ndadaye in 1993.
